title: Vendor Layout Spillover: Does Adjacency Confound the Market-Day Effect on Sales?
one_line: Use instrumental-variable-like reasoning on sparse, non-random vendor placement to separate the causal effect of foot traffic (day-of-week) from locational advantage, where standard causal adjustment fails because treatment is spatially embedded.
self_assessment: Has legs: the tension between observational causal inference (built for independent units) and spatial-network data (where treatment and confounders are entangled by geography) forces a genuine methodological compromise that exposes the limits of covariate adjustment.

title: Temporal Hypergraph Collapse: Detecting Brood-Pattern Asymmetries via Time-Windowed Subgraph Isomorphism
one_line: Can we detect early colony disease spread by comparing observed nurse→brood contact networks against the null model of 'symmetric diffusion,' where the technique fails unless we collapse temporal hyperedges into directed time-lagged digraphs?
self_assessment: The seam is real: standard network analysis treats contacts as undirected snapshots, but brood disease propagation is causal (nurse→brood, not vice versa) and time-indexed; we must engineer directed lagged edges from temporal contact sequences. This forces explicit handling of the temporal asymmetry rather than applying off-the-shelf centrality.

title: Thrift Price Clusters Under Measurement Error: Can k-means recover categories when item descriptions are noisy proxies for condition?
one_line: Apply k-means clustering to price × text-derived condition features on thrift items, but force the algorithm to work with *deliberately degraded* condition labels (truncation, OCR-style noise) to test whether market-meaningful clusters emerge despite the feature being corrupted—revealing the tension between what clustering needs (clean features) and what thrift data supplies (sparse, error-prone metadata).
self_assessment: This has legs because the core tension (clustering assumes latent clean structure, but thrift pricing is driven by messy grading systems) forces a methodological compromise: either you admit the cluster labels don't align with ground truth, or you ask what structure survives *despite* noise—which is honest and uncommon in tutorial examples.

title: Beekeeper Log Variance Decay: Inferring Inspection Fatigue from NLP Coherence Drift
one_line: Does the *linguistic consistency* of beekeeper inspection logs degrade predictably over a season, and can that decay signal colony stress better than the explicit observations recorded?
self_assessment: This has legs: NLP on logs assumes static vocabulary/style, but beekeepers' logs naturally drift in precision, detail, and reference consistency as fatigue or attention shifts. That drift itself—measured as token-sequence entropy or semantic coherence within rolling windows—becomes a signal. The insight is that the *noise floor* of the writing is more stable and informative than the surface content.

title: Vendor Revenue Stability via Isolation Forest on Compositional Sales Data
one_line: Can isolation forest detect destabilized vendors by treating item-category revenue shares as a simplex, where traditional anomaly detection fails because it ignores the sum-to-one constraint that defines market behavior?
self_assessment: This has legs: the core insight is that anomaly detection on compositional data (proportions summing to 1) breaks standard distance metrics, and forcing iso-forest to work on the simplex requires either log-ratio transformation or a custom metric—revealing why anomalies in *budget allocation* across categories (not just total revenue) signal real vendor stress.

title: Trail Bottleneck Detection via Temporal Hypergraph Switching
one_line: Can we detect trail segments where hiker flow transitions from parallel to sequential (bottlenecks) by collapsing GPS trajectory hyperedges into time-lagged directed graphs, forcing the technique to handle continuous paths as discrete switching events?
self_assessment: This has genuine friction: standard graph_network_analysis assumes nodes and edges are pre-defined, but trail data arrives as continuous trajectories (hyperedges spanning many GPS points). The insight is that bottlenecks aren't structural—they're behavioral regime shifts in the *temporal* edge-formation process, requiring us to bin time windows and detect when the digraph transitions from high out-degree (parallel dispersal) to low out-degree (forced serialization). That modification is the technique, not window dressing.

title: Demand Reversal Detection in Community Theater Box Office via Isolation Forest on Ticket-Category Co-Purchase Anomalies
one_line: Can isolation forest detect when the typical pairing structure of ticket-category purchases breaks down (e.g., when usually-bundled seats sell independently), signaling hidden demand shifts or pricing misalignment that raw per-category sales don't expose?
self_assessment: This forces isolation forest to operate on a compositional simplex (ticket-category mix per transaction) where the anomaly isn't high/low volume but structural *change in co-purchase ratios*, requiring the detector to see that same-day transactions suddenly decouple from historical pairing patterns—real theater data would show this during cast changes, venue reconfiguration, or dynamic pricing, making it a genuine domain friction point.

title: Entailment Drift in Beekeeper Inspection Logs: Detecting Colony Decline via NLP Premise-Hypothesis Collapse
one_line: Can we detect colony decline by measuring whether beekeeper observations *logically entail* expected health conclusions less reliably over time, treating inspection logs as defeasible reasoning chains that weaken under stress?
self_assessment: This forces NLP beyond sentiment/classification: logs are treated as mini-arguments where premise (observations) should entail hypothesis (health status), and that relationship degrades under colony stress—a genuine mismatch between log structure (causal narratives) and standard NLP tasks (labels or bags-of-words).

title: Pollinator Isolation in Garden Networks: Detecting Crop-Specific Connectivity Collapse
one_line: Can we detect when a garden plot's flowering schedule creates isolation in the pollinator-visitation network—where graph centrality collapses not because plots are deleted, but because flowering *timing* desynchronizes the edge structure?
self_assessment: The genuine tension: standard node/edge removal doesn't model garden dynamics; we must redefine edges as time-windowed flowering overlaps, forcing the network to be *reconstructed* at each week. This breaks traditional centrality assumptions and reveals when scheduling creates de-facto isolation despite physical proximity.

title: Plot Yield Forecast Under Crop Rotation Structural Break
one_line: Can we forecast next-season plot yield when crop rotation causes the covariate-to-yield relationship to abruptly invert, forcing the forecaster to detect and adapt to regime shifts in a domain where the causal structure changes by definition?
self_assessment: This has real legs: the tension is genuine—standard forecasting assumes stationarity, but crop rotation *intentionally breaks* the feature-to-target relationship. The forecaster must detect this structural break, not just fit trend. Most garden forecasts ignore rotation; this one treats rotation-induced non-stationarity as the core problem.

title: QSO Duration Clustering Under Scheduling Constraint Collapse
one_line: Can bin-packing heuristics for contest time-slot allocation detect mode-switching behavior (contest vs. ragchew) when QSO duration distributions are bimodal and the packing itself forces misclassification of marginal cases?
self_assessment: This has legs: the tension is real—optimization schedulers assume unimodal task durations, but amateur radio logs exhibit persistent bimodal structure (short contestQSOs vs. long rag-chew conversations). The interesting bit is that *forcing* a bin-packing solver to minimize idle time on a mixed-mode duration stream makes the solver a mode-detector: it will cluster durations not to recover ground truth but to pack efficiently, revealing which operators were actually ragchewin in a contest-logged session.

title: Temporal Clustering Collapse in Community Theater Demand: Do Purchase Sequences Reveal Hidden Show-Type Segments When Arrival Timing Is the Primary Feature?
one_line: Can clustering on *inter-purchase arrival times* (not revenue, not seat location) recover latent show-type segments when traditional categorical clustering fails because the domain naturally encodes preference in *when* people buy, not *what* they buy?
self_assessment: This has teeth: the insight is that community theater demand is *sequential*—families buy together days in advance, while walk-ups and subscription renewals arrive minutes apart—and clustering on temporal spacing rather than ticket type forces the algorithm to discover audience *behavior modes* hidden in the timing microstructure. The seam is real: standard clustering assumes features, but here the feature engineering itself is the discovery.

title: Multiplayer Session Duration Forecasting Under Inventory Coupling
one_line: Can ARIMA forecast multiplayer game session duration when the covariate (inventory availability of complementary games) creates feedback—unavailable games shorten sessions, which frees inventory, which lengthens future sessions—forcing the forecaster to handle endogenous coupling instead of exogenous regressors?
self_assessment: Has real teeth: standard forecasting assumes regressors are exogenous, but inventory-constrained domains have inventory *levels driven by the quantity being forecast*, creating simultaneity bias that requires structural detection or differencing, not just lag-augmentation.

title: Game-Slot Imbalance Detection in Little League Schedules via Isolation Forest on Fixture Timing Skew
one_line: Can isolation forest detect scheduling inequities by treating each team's distribution of game start times and opponent difficulty as a multivariate point, where traditional fairness metrics fail because they ignore the nonlinear coupling between slot scarcity and team exposure?
self_assessment: This has real legs: isolation forest is built to find points in feature space that don't cluster with peers, but little-league fairness requires detecting when a *team's aggregated exposure* (to prime time slots + strong opponents) deviates from the population norm—a shape that isolation forest can surface without needing a fairness-specific loss function, revealing hidden biases that slot-counting methods miss.
